reference.source: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
clinicalPearls: An autosomal dominant disorder caused by loss-of-function variants in EXT1 or EXT2, encoding enzymes for heparan sulphate biosynthesis
Characterised by multiple osteochondromas (exostoses) arising from the metaphyses of long bones, ribs, scapulae and pelvis, typically capped by cartilage and pointing away from the joint
Lesions appear in childhood, enlarge during growth and characteristically stop growing after skeletal maturity
Common complications include limb-length discrepancy, forearm deformity (ulnar shortening/bowing with radial head dislocation), genu valgum and coxa valga
Osteochondromas can cause pain, mechanical restriction, bursitis or compression of adjacent nerves, vessels or tendons
The most important long-term risk is malignant transformation of an osteochondroma to secondary chondrosarcoma, more likely with axial/proximal lesions
New pain, growth of a lesion after skeletal maturity, or a thickened cartilage cap should prompt evaluation for malignant transformation
reference.pathophysiology: Multiple hereditary exostoses is caused by inactivating variants in EXT1 or EXT2, which encode glycosyltransferases that synthesise heparan sulphate. Heparan sulphate proteoglycans regulate the diffusion and signalling of morphogens such as Indian hedgehog in the growth plate. Deficient heparan sulphate disrupts the normal polarity and containment of proliferating chondrocytes at the perichondrium, so ectopic cartilage-capped bony outgrowths (osteochondromas) form at the metaphyses and grow by endochondral ossification. Malignant transformation reflects additional somatic events within the cartilage cap.
additionalInvestigations: Skeletal survey to map the number, size and distribution of osteochondromas
Cross-sectional imaging (MRI) to measure cartilage cap thickness when transformation is suspected
Targeted imaging of forearm, knees and hips to assess deformity and joint mechanics
Neurovascular assessment where a lesion compresses adjacent structures
redFlags: Growth of a lesion or new pain after skeletal maturity suggesting malignant transformation
A thickened cartilage cap on imaging concerning for secondary chondrosarcoma
Neurovascular compromise or spinal cord compression from an osteochondroma
Rapidly enlarging axial or pelvic lesions with the highest transformation risk
reference.prognosis: Most people have a normal lifespan with orthopaedic morbidity from deformity and mechanical complications; the principal serious risk is secondary chondrosarcoma in a minority, making lifelong surveillance for malignant transformation important.
pitfalls: Reassuring a patient about a lesion that has grown after skeletal maturity, when this is a warning sign
Failing to arrange surveillance for malignant transformation, especially of axial lesions
Overlooking forearm deformity and radial head dislocation that benefit from timely orthopaedic correction
Confusing the diagnosis with enchondromatosis, which involves intramedullary rather than surface cartilage lesions
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
management: No drug therapy alters osteochondroma formation; management is orthopaedic, with surgical excision of symptomatic lesions causing pain, mechanical restriction or neurovascular and tendon compression
Corrective surgery for forearm deformity, limb-length discrepancy and angular deformity such as genu valgum, using osteotomy, guided growth or limb reconstruction
Lifelong surveillance for malignant transformation to secondary chondrosarcoma, with particular attention to axial and proximal lesions
Cross-sectional MRI to measure cartilage-cap thickness, prompting excision when a lesion grows after skeletal maturity or becomes painful
Neurovascular assessment and decompression where an exostosis compresses adjacent nerves or vessels
Genetic counselling for autosomal dominant EXT1/EXT2 inheritance, with cascade testing and clinical assessment of relatives
Escalate to a specialist bone-tumour (sarcoma) service when malignant transformation is suspected
